findings.title: The reader is the largest variable
findings.body: On the same graph Utopia's chat got 2 of 10 right and Opus with all tools got 9. Arm A measured Utopia's reference chat loop, not the foundation; Utopia's own ADR 0046 says the app surface is MCP.

findings.title: A strong reader did the OWM's work at question time
findings.body: B1 composed role + reporting line + policy band into the approver, kept eligibility apart from authority, chose policy and exception by date, refused hearsay and matched ids on DUNS. The OWM's case must rest on what that lacks: persistence, consistency and audit, scale, cost.

findings.title: Every reporting line is inverted
findings.body: Utopia's MCP serves `Michael Torres —reports to→ Sarah Chen` and `David Morgan —reports to→ Michael Torres`, citing organization_chart.md: the indented list was read upside down.

findings.title: The reader usually repairs foundation errors silently
findings.body: Utopia serves every reporting edge inverted. In most B2 answers the reader wrote "Sarah reports to Michael" from title priors without comment; in 3 of 60 it flagged the edge as reversed. Right answer, wrong data, usually invisible. Candidate OWM capability: structural constraints on organizational relations that flag the error.

findings.title: Authority and eligibility values never reached the graph
findings.body: No VP Sales band (>10% ≤20%), no percentages as values, undated roles. The current 15% exception is undated while the stale 10% one is dated, so dated reads find the past and miss the present.

findings.title: Every CSV lost rows to truncated extraction
findings.body: All six CSVs hit `truncated_reply`; rows after the cut produced no facts. Structured evidence is the least completely extracted part of the corpus.

findings.title: Graph tools carry quotes, but only through `changes`
findings.body: `entity_facts` returns document ids, not quotes. B2 reached the percentages only by calling `changes` per entity since ingestion day, an audit feed used as a quote retriever.

findings.title: Identity is decided on names, and the stakes are routed backwards
findings.body: The adjudicator never used shared DUNS, SKU or email. It auto-applied the identity calls that change answers at 90–95% and sent SKU trivia to humans.

findings.title: Utopia's chat confuses record time with world time
findings.body: It passed question dates as `as_of` (record time), before anything was ingested, so every lookup was empty. It also invented "100%" for S06b.

findings.title: Identity review bought nothing measurable
findings.body: B1 was unchanged after 18 corrections. B2's binding gaps are missing facts, which no identity decision can supply and the Review queue never surfaces.

findings.title: A human merge erased the identifier it connected
findings.body: Merging C-1001 and CRM-2048 into Acme dropped them as findable names: the ID entities had a canonical name but no name fact. Appears to diverge from Utopia ADR 0041 decision 1.

findings.title: The graph-only drop after correction is real, not variance
findings.body: n = 3 on each side, same KBs, reader and questions. Pre-correction B2 grades 6/4/0, 6/4/0, 5/4/1; post-correction 4/3/3, 4/3/3, 4/4/2. The earlier "reader-strategy variance" reading was wrong.

findings.title: Cleaner identity cut the dig that found the evidence
findings.body: On S01, S02 and S04 the reader dug through per-entity `changes` in 8 of 9 pre-correction runs and 0 of 9 post-correction (Fisher p ≈ 0.0002). S04 is right exactly when it dug. The correction changed reader behaviour; the "consolidated entities look complete" mechanism is inferred from traces. Graph-only answers ride on an undocumented path: the fix is quotes on `entity_facts`, not identity review.

findings.title: Curating facts fixed the authority questions
findings.body: With the approval bands, exception values and reporting lines curated as graph facts, graph-only B2 graded 7/2/1 in all three runs (vs 4/3/3 uncurated). S01, S02 and S04 were right every time, read straight from `entity_facts` with no `changes` dig, in ~30% fewer turns. The gap was missing facts, not reader reasoning.

findings.title: Complete authority facts made the missing-evidence case worse
findings.body: In the missing-contract KB, curated bands let the reader approve DR-9001 "with Michael's sign-off" in 3 of 3 runs, never asking whether the contract exists (uncurated it declined). More facts without the decision procedure (check contract and exception before authority, doc 03 §11) produce a confident wrong answer. The procedure and its evidence requirements belong to the OWM.

findings.title: Writing facts back to Utopia is an identity review
findings.body: The Statements contract takes names, not entity ids. The pilot's exact names created new Sarah Chen and Michael Torres entities, queued for a human at 0.52-0.54; the full push attached most names directly but not all, and raised two new candidate pairs. An OWM that writes back must pass through review for every write, or treat the foundation as read-only evidence.

findings.title: The decision procedure closes the gap
findings.body: Adding the organization's own procedure (the corpus SOP + doc 03 §11, now owm/procedures/discount-approval.md) to the blind graph-only reader on curated facts: S01–S04 pass the automatic answer-key check in 3 of 3 runs, S03 is fully right (REVIEW_REQUIRED) for the first time in any condition, and S05 returns REQUEST_EVIDENCE in 2 of 3. Runs grade 8/1/1, 9/1/0, 9/1/0, level with the full-text reader (B1 9/1/0). Facts plus procedure, not a stronger reader, is what the boundary needs.

findings.title: The last S05 miss is a missing request record
findings.body: All three S05 runs found the request's basis 'unknown' and listed the contract as missing evidence; one assumed standard pricing and approved. The graph lost DR-9001's own row (justification: 'Contract pricing per Acme MSA') to CSV truncation. An OWM decision needs the request record with its stated basis, from the CRM, as a first-class input.
